race:orc.title: Orcs
race:orc.summary: Big, proud and loud, with tusks and tempers to match. Orcs come from the red steppe, where the drums remember every name and the storm carries the ancestors.

sections.title: Who they are
sections.text: Orcs live about eighty years, hard ones. They are taller and stronger than humans, quicker to anger and quicker to forgive, and they value courage, loyalty and a good story above everything. Other peoples think orcs are simple. Orcs let them think so, and win the bet.

sections.title: Where they live
sections.text: On the [[place:red-steppe|red steppe]], in clans that follow their herds. The [[culture:orc.bloodfang|Bloodfang]] are its berserkers, the [[culture:orc.stormcaller|Stormcallers]] its shamans, and the [[culture:orc.ashland|Ashlanders]] the survivors who made a life in the burned wastes. Since the [[era:great-burn|Great Burn]], many orcs also live in human cities, which they find too quiet.

sections.title: The drums
sections.text: Orcs write little down. The drums keep their history: every clan has a rhythm, every great deed a beat, every name a pattern. An orc who earns a war-name has it added to the clan's drums, and is remembered for as long as anyone plays them.

sections.title: Among the Pact
sections.text: Marak Thunderhide of the [[era:first-five|First Five]] was a Stormcaller shaman. Orcs joined the [[faction:pact|Pact]] in great numbers after the Great Burn, when the last Great Muster closed the Ashmaw, and many of today's orc heroes are children of that year.

facts: The red steppe and the Ashlands
Bloodfury: below half health, Might and Arcana count 10% higher
quote: A scar is a lesson you can wear.

heritage:orc.title: Orcish Heritage
heritage:orc.summary: Orcish heritage is beaten on the drums: the clan's rhythm, the war-names of its heroes, the deeds of its dead. Renown is a louder beat, and it grows fastest when clanmates see you earn it.

sections.title: War-names
sections.text: An orc is born with a name and earns a war-name. Every deed that reaches the drums makes the beat louder, and when kin fight together the drummers hear about it from more than one mouth. Orcs say the ancestors listen to the drums, so Renown is also how loudly the dead know your name.

heritage:orc.trunk0.title: Thick Skull
heritage:orc.trunk0.summary: Orcs have survived the steppe, the Burn and each other. A thick skull is a family heirloom.

heritage:orc.trunk1.title: War Drums
heritage:orc.trunk1.summary: The rhythm of the clan drums, which every orc hears in battle whether there is a drummer or not.

heritage:orc.trunk2.title: Sagas
heritage:orc.trunk2.summary: The beats of the clan drums, which carry your war-name. Every deed beaten into them brings more Renown.

heritage:orc.bloodfang0.title: Bloodlust
heritage:orc.bloodfang0.summary: The Bloodfang's red joy in battle, which grows with every wound given and taken.

heritage:orc.bloodfang1.title: Charge
heritage:orc.bloodfang1.summary: The Bloodfang charge is the most feared sight on the steppe: a line of orcs that does not stop.

heritage:orc.bloodfang2.title: Bloodfang Kinship
heritage:orc.bloodfang2.summary: Bloodfang orcs fight as a warband. Two of them in a band share one battle-fury.

heritage:orc.stormcaller0.title: Spirit Talk
heritage:orc.stormcaller0.summary: The shaman's gift of hearing the ancestors, who whisper where the next blow will fall.

heritage:orc.stormcaller1.title: Rain Dance
heritage:orc.stormcaller1.summary: The dance that calls the rain, and with it the healing of the ancestors.

heritage:orc.stormcaller2.title: Stormcallers Kinship
heritage:orc.stormcaller2.summary: Stormcallers call the storm together. With two in one band, the ancestors answer louder.

heritage:orc.ashland0.title: Ashen Hide
heritage:orc.ashland0.summary: Skin toughened by ash storms and hot ground, that shrugs off what would burn others.

heritage:orc.ashland1.title: Hard Living
heritage:orc.ashland1.summary: Ashlanders survive on nothing. That makes them very hard to wear down.

heritage:orc.ashland2.title: Ashlanders Kinship
heritage:orc.ashland2.summary: On the ash caravans every hand counts. Two Ashlanders in a band carry each other.

culture:orc.bloodfang.title: Bloodfang
culture:orc.bloodfang.summary: The great warrior clans of the western steppe: riders, pit fighters and berserkers, who believe the best way to honour the ancestors is to join them gloriously, but not too soon.

sections.title: The clans
sections.text: The Bloodfang hold the richest grazing on the [[place:red-steppe|red steppe]] and the most blood pits. They ride wolves, raid each other, and settle every argument in the pits for meat and glory. When the [[faction:nine-clans|Nine Clans]] unite, it is usually under a Bloodfang warchief.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Bloodfang orcs are fighters first and everything else second. Their whelps wrestle before they walk, pass the blood trial young, and earn war-names in the pits. They are also fiercely loyal and laugh more than any other orcs, usually at something painful.

sections.title: The red fury
sections.text: Bloodfang berserkers fight in a red fury that makes them stronger the more they bleed. Elders teach that the fury is a gift from the ancestors, and that a gift used carelessly can be taken back.

quote: Bleed well, and the drums will forgive you anything.

culture:orc.stormcaller.title: Stormcallers
culture:orc.stormcaller.kicker: Shamans who speak with the ancestors
culture:orc.stormcaller.summary: The shaman clans of the thunder hills, who hear the ancestors in the storm, dance the rain down and keep the clan totems.

sections.title: The hills
sections.text: In the north of the [[place:red-steppe|steppe]], low hills catch every storm that crosses it. The Stormcallers live there, where the thunder is loudest, because they believe it is the [[faith:ancestors|ancestors]] arguing, and someone has to listen.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Stormcaller orcs are shamans, totem-keepers and rain-callers. They are quieter than the Bloodfang and more frightening, because they know things. Their shamans foresaw the [[era:great-burn|Great Burn]] years before it came, and nobody listened.

sections.title: Marak's people
sections.text: Marak Thunderhide of the [[era:first-five|First Five]] was a Stormcaller. His spirit is said to ride at the front of every storm, and Stormcallers who swear the [[faction:pact|Pact]] carve his name on their totems.

facts: A hand raised to the sky
quote: When the ancestors go quiet, start running.

culture:orc.ashland.title: Ashlanders
culture:orc.ashland.summary: The orcs who live in the Ashlands: scavengers, caravan guards and survivors, who take in anyone who can carry a load and leave nobody behind in a storm.

sections.title: The wastes
sections.text: The [[place:ashlands|Ashlands]] grew by half after the [[era:great-burn|Great Burn]], and many clans who lost their grazing walked into them. The ones who lived became the Ashlanders, a people made out of every clan and none.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Ashlanders are tough, practical and generous with everything but water. They run caravans of salt and ash-iron across the wastes, guard them against [[beast:shadow-beasts|shadow-beasts]], and have one law above all: on the caravan, every hand counts. It is the Pact's fourth rule, and Ashlanders say they had it first.

sections.title: Unkillable
sections.text: Ashlanders who walked out of ash storms alone, or survived the Burn when their clans did not, are held in awe. They do not like to talk about it.

backstory:orc.pitfighter.title: Pit Fighter
backstory:orc.pitfighter.summary: Fought in the Bloodfang blood pits for meat and glory, and has the scars and the stories to prove it.

sections.title: The pits
sections.text: The blood pits of the [[culture:orc.bloodfang|Bloodfang]] settle disputes, train whelps and entertain everyone else. A pit fighter learns that the crowd loves a fighter who keeps getting up.

backstory:orc.outrider.title: Steppe Outrider
backstory:orc.outrider.summary: Rode ahead of the horde on the red steppe, scouting the grass for enemies and herds.

sections.title: Outriders
sections.text: Bloodfang outriders ride days ahead of the clan on wolves or ponies. They are the eyes of the horde, and the first to die when it goes wrong.

backstory:orc.warband.title: Warband-born
backstory:orc.warband.summary: Born on the march and raised by the whole warband, which counts everyone as kin.

sections.title: The warband
sections.text: A Bloodfang warband on the march is a moving village. Whelps born there are raised by everyone and taught by whoever is nearest.

backstory:orc.spiritchild.title: Spirit-touched
backstory:orc.spiritchild.summary: Heard the ancestors whisper before they could speak, and the Stormcallers noticed at once.

sections.title: The touched
sections.text: The [[culture:orc.stormcaller|Stormcallers]] take any whelp who hears the ancestors early. It is a gift, and a weight: the ancestors rarely say pleasant things.

backstory:orc.raincaller.title: Rain-caller
backstory:orc.raincaller.summary: Danced the rain dance that broke a seven-year drought, and the clan has not forgotten it.

sections.title: The rain dance
sections.text: Stormcaller rain dances last from dusk to dawn. Most fail. One that brings rain after a long drought makes the dancer a legend for life.

backstory:orc.totemkeeper.title: Totem-keeper
backstory:orc.totemkeeper.summary: Kept the clan totem and the names carved on it, every one of them.

sections.title: The totem
sections.text: Every Stormcaller clan carves the names of its dead on a great wooden totem. Its keeper knows every name and every story, and carries the totem when the clan moves.

backstory:orc.scavenger.title: Ash Scavenger
backstory:orc.scavenger.summary: Survived the burned wastes on what others left behind, and knows the value of everything.

sections.title: Scavenging
sections.text: The [[place:ashlands|Ashlands]] are littered with the ruins of the Elderwood and the wreckage of the Burn. Scavengers know where to dig, and what not to touch.

backstory:orc.survivor.title: Last Survivor
backstory:orc.survivor.summary: Walked out of the ash storm alone and lived, when nobody else did.

sections.title: The ones who walk out
sections.text: Ashlanders honour those who walk out of storms alone, and never ask what happened in them.

backstory:orc.caravan.title: Caravan Guard
backstory:orc.caravan.summary: Guarded the ash caravans across the wastes, where every hand counts and nobody is left behind.

sections.title: The caravans
sections.text: Ashlander caravans carry salt and ash-iron across the wastes to the cities. Their guards fight shadow-beasts, raiders and storms, and the Pact recruits them gladly.

answer:orc.grandparents.0.summary: The last warchief who united nine clans did it for a single summer. That summer is still the favourite song at every fire.

answer:orc.grandparents.1.summary: The Stormcaller shamans foresaw the Great Burn years before it came. Nobody listened.

answer:orc.grandparents.2.summary: Orc peacemakers who made treaties with the human lands were called cowards for it. After the Burn, those treaties fed whole clans.

answer:orc.grandparents.3.summary: The wolf-riders of the Bloodfang raise their wolves from cubs. Losing one is mourned like a clanmate.

answer:orc.parents.0.summary: Steppe hunters follow the great aurochs herds. In lean years, the clan lives or dies by them.

answer:orc.parents.1.summary: Black iron is worked from ore found near Hollows, and makes the heaviest blades on the steppe.

answer:orc.parents.2.summary: Orc storytellers carry the clan's tale from fire to fire, so that every clan knows every other's honour.

answer:orc.parents.3.summary: Orphans of battle are raised by the whole clan, and grow up as the clan's own.

answer:orc.siblings.0.summary: Orc litters fight for everything, and the bonds that come out of those fights are for life.

answer:orc.siblings.1.summary: Orcs say the clever ones are born small so the strong ones learn to protect something.

answer:orc.siblings.2.summary: War-pups are the orphans of the clan's battles, raised together and fiercely loyal to each other.

answer:orc.siblings.3.summary: Tame boars are common in orc camps, and more reliable than most watch-dogs.

answer:orc.birth.0.summary: A blood moon is ill luck on the steppe, and the elders' sign against it is the oldest gesture orcs know.

answer:orc.birth.1.summary: Thunder without rain means the ancestors are arguing about someone. The shamans pay attention to who is born under it.

answer:orc.birth.2.summary: A lone wolf howling at a birth tent is said to be an ancestor come to see the newborn.

answer:orc.birth.3.summary: Ash falls on the steppe when the Ashlands burn. Children born under it are said to belong to the wastes.

answer:orc.friend.0.summary: Wolf cubs raised by whelps become their mounts. The bond between them is the strongest on the steppe.

answer:orc.friend.1.summary: Human captives taken in raids sometimes stay with the clans. Some of them taught orcs to read.

answer:orc.friend.2.summary: Shaman apprentices hear the spirits young, and many are frightened of the dark for exactly that reason.

answer:orc.friend.3.summary: Truces between rival clans are held at sacred stones. Friendships made there are never spoken of.

answer:orc.play.0.summary: Orc whelps wrestle constantly. It is how they learn who to follow and who to protect.

answer:orc.play.1.summary: Every clan has a drum rhythm, and every whelp who can keep it is given a drum of their own.

answer:orc.play.2.summary: Steppe tracking starts with rabbits and ends, for the best, with the trail of a Hollow's beasts.

answer:orc.play.3.summary: The steppe winds blow hard enough to race. The best young runners become outriders.

answer:orc.teen.0.summary: The blood trial tests every young orc: a night alone on the steppe, and a beast brought back at dawn.

answer:orc.teen.1.summary: Failing the blood trial once is no shame. Not coming back for the second one is.

answer:orc.teen.2.summary: The shaman's path is the only honourable way to turn from the blood trial, and the harder of the two.

answer:orc.teen.3.summary: Clanless outcasts roam the steppe's edge. A year among them teaches what a clan is worth.

answer:orc.firstfight.0.summary: Human patrols from the Crownlands sometimes ride too far east. Orcs consider this a gift.

answer:orc.firstfight.1.summary: Sand-wyrms swim under the dry southern grass and eat whole herds. Their hide makes the best armour on the steppe.

answer:orc.firstfight.2.summary: Insults to a mother are settled in the pits, and the fight is remembered longer than the insult.

answer:orc.firstfight.3.summary: Saving a rival creates a debt orcs can never mention and never forget.

answer:orc.mentor.0.summary: One-eyed veterans are everywhere on the steppe, and the best teachers, because they know what it costs.

answer:orc.mentor.1.summary: The clan shaman speaks for the ancestors, and the ancestors speak mostly in riddles.

answer:orc.mentor.2.summary: Human prisoners have taught orcs more about the world than any envoy.

answer:orc.mentor.3.summary: Hunger is the oldest teacher on the steppe, and after the Burn, the commonest.

answer:orc.leaving.0.summary: Sparing an enemy the chief wants dead is mercy to some clans and treason to others.

answer:orc.leaving.1.summary: War-names earned in the Pact's Hollows are beaten on the drums like any other. Some of the loudest are.

answer:orc.leaving.2.summary: Orc envoys to the cities often stay, because the cities need them more than they admit.

answer:orc.leaving.3.summary: The Great Burn left whole clans with nowhere to stay. Many of their children are now Pact heroes.

answer:orc.deed.0.summary: Great boars of the steppe kill hunters every year. Slaying one earns a war-name on its own.

answer:orc.deed.1.summary: Blood feuds can last generations. Ending one is harder than winning one, and more honoured.

answer:orc.deed.2.summary: Rain dances that break a drought are the Stormcallers' greatest deeds.

answer:orc.deed.3.summary: The great wolf race crosses the red steppe from west to east every five years, and only half the riders finish.

answer:orc.loss.0.summary: Orcs carry a fallen war-brother's tusk so the ancestors can find them both.

answer:orc.loss.1.summary: Since the Burn, scattered clans are common, and orcs who lost theirs often find a new one in the Pact.

answer:orc.loss.2.summary: The red rage is a gift and a danger. Every orc who has lost control of it has someone to mourn.

answer:orc.loss.3.summary: The shamans say luck that lasts too long is the ancestors saving something for later.

answer:orc.fear.0.summary: Dying old in bed is the worst death orcs can imagine, because the ancestors might not notice.

answer:orc.fear.1.summary: An orc who calls on the ancestors and hears nothing has lost them, and nothing on the steppe is lonelier.

answer:orc.fear.2.summary: The red fury of the Bloodfang can turn on friends as easily as foes.

answer:orc.fear.3.summary: The Chain Lords put captives in cages on wheels. Orcs who were caged never forget the walls.

answer:orc.keepsake.0.summary: A fallen friend's tusk on a cord lets the ancestors know who you are carrying.

answer:orc.keepsake.1.summary: Small clan drums carry the clan's rhythm anywhere, and are beaten at every victory.

answer:orc.keepsake.2.summary: Spirit fetishes are blessed by the shaman so the ancestors can find their wearer far from the steppe.

answer:orc.keepsake.3.summary: Human books are prized by orcs who learned to read. Finishing one is a quiet victory.

answer:orc.drive.0.summary: Glory is what the drums beat for, and the Pact's Hollows offer more of it than any raid.

answer:orc.drive.1.summary: Since the Burn, clans without land wander. Finding them a home is the dream of many orc heroes.

answer:orc.drive.2.summary: Orc healers, scholars and shamans are proving the old ways wrong in every band of the Pact.

answer:orc.drive.3.summary: Vengeance is honoured on the steppe, but the Pact has a rule about leaving nobody behind, and it applies to enemies too.
